origin.description: Build a function that sets state, runs code, and restores the state.

arguments.name: set
arguments.text: Callable that installs the new state and returns the old one.

arguments.name: reset
arguments.text: Callable that restores the old state.

arguments.name: get
arguments.text: Optional callable that reads the old state before set.

arguments.name: new
arguments.text: When false, the built function takes code first.

origin.details: code is a callable. R forces the expression after set, which is why the translation cannot take an already-computed value. Extra arguments of set follow code.
origin.example:
res <- integer()
set <- function(new) res <<- c(res, 1L)
reset <- function(old) res <<- c(res, 3L)
body <- function() res <<- c(res, 2L)
fn <- with_(set, reset)
fn(NULL, body())
res
